newsitem.title: UK: Energy Group in PacifiCorp's sights.
newsitem.headline: Energy Group in PacifiCorp's sights.

text.p: Britain's Energy Group Plc, which demerged from conglomerate Hanson only in February, said on Tuesday it is in talks with PacifiCorp of the United States which may lead to a recommended offer being made for it.

The group, Britain's biggest electricity distributor, said in a statement that any offer would be expected to be priced at a premium of around 20 percent to the company's closing share price on the London Stock Exchange of 5.80 pounds ($9.49).
At 5.80 pounds per share, the group is valued at around three billion pounds.
"I'm not surprised that talks have been taking place," said Nigel Hawkins, analyst with Yamaichi. "(Energy Group) is one of few relatively vertically integrated utilities in the UK".

Energy Group owns Eastern Electricity, a regional electricity supplier, and is Britain's fourth biggest generator after buying 6,000 megaWatts of capacity from National Power and PowerGen. It also owns the U.S. coal business Peabody Resources Ltd.
"It was seen from all that...as being quite an attractive takeover target post its demerger from Hanson," Hawkins added.

Energy Group, which had been due to report its results for the six months to March 31 on Thursday, said it would not now be releasing the figures until the outcome of its talks with PacifiCorp had been settled.
It said a further announcement, to include the results, would be issued "as soon as practicable".
Energy Group announced the talks with PacifiCorp following a recent jump in the company's share price. It had gained 18-1/2 pence to Tuesday's 5.80 pound close.
Hawkins said the price was likely to firm to the 6.50 to 7.00 pounds area when the London Stock Market reopens on Wednesday.

He said the only clouds on the horizon might be some "regulatory concerns" over the takeover and the uncertainty about any windfall tax the new Labour government might impose on the group's Eastern Electricity unit.
Eastern Electricity was one of the 12 regional electricity companies privatised by the former Conservative government.
There was also a question mark over whether PacifiCorp would be prepared to pay the 20 percent premium to the 5.80 pound closing price.
"The outcome of these discussion will be awaited with considerable impatience," Hawkins said. ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
